bench_setup = function() {
  set.seed(20261117)
  n = 200L
  w = rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)
  Z = matrix(rnorm(n * 3L), n, 3L, dimnames = list(NULL, c("x1", "x2", "x3")))
  y = 1 + 0.5 * w + as.numeric(Z %*% c(0.4, -0.3, 0.2)) + rnorm(n)
  out_idx = sample.int(n, 10L)
  y[out_idx] = y[out_idx] + 8   # 5% vertical outliers
  X = cbind("(Intercept)" = 1, w = w, Z)
  df = data.frame(y = y, w = w, Z)
  list(X = X, y = y, df = df)
}
notes: Times one fit at n = 200, p = 5 (intercept, treatment, 3 covariates) with 5% vertical outliers: EDI's bisquare-M from an LS start vs RobStatTM's deterministic Pena-Yohai-start MM (bisquare, 95% efficiency, matching EDI's c = 4.685). This is an estimator change and the finding itself expects the candidate to be slower (it competes with FAST-S, not with today's path), so the useful output is the ratio; expected verdict 'not faster'. tol 0.15 allows the S-scale vs MAD-scale difference on clean-ish data; a larger gap means the two estimators genuinely disagree.
